original_question: For integers 4<=t<=n, let g_{K_t}(n) be the maximum size of a family of graphs on vertex set [n] such that the intersection of any two graphs in the family contains a copy of the complete graph K_t. Determine whether g_{K_t}(n)=2^{C(n,2)-C(t,2)} for all such t and n.
target_in_paper: Section 4, Conjecture 4.1 (the clique case of the H-intersecting-family problem).
correct_elements: Your draft matches Conjecture 4.1 very closely: it uses the same parameter range 4≤t≤n, the same extremal quantity g_{K_t}(n), the same ambient object (families of graphs on [n]), the same K_t-intersection condition, and the exact conjectured value 2^{\binom{n}{2}-\binom{t}{2}}.
missing_details: Specify that [n]={1,2,...,n} and that all graphs are simple labelled graphs on this common vertex set.
State explicitly that K_t is the complete graph on t vertices and that 'contains a copy of K_t' means as a subgraph (not necessarily induced).

Use the paper’s quantifier 'for all G_1,G_2 in F' rather than the potentially ambiguous phrase 'any two graphs'; in the paper this includes the case G_1=G_2, so each graph in F itself must contain a K_t.
If you want the formulation to mirror the paper exactly, note that this is the specialization H=K_t of the general definition g_H(n):=max{|F|: F is an H-intersecting family of graphs on [n]}.
For paper-faithful nearby context, note that the paper records that Conjecture 4.1 has already been proved for t=4, so the genuinely open cases there are t≥5.
refined_question: For integers t,n with 4≤t≤n, let [n]:={1,2,...,n}, let K_t denote the complete graph on t vertices, and let g_{K_t}(n) be the maximum size of a family F of simple labelled graphs on the common vertex set [n] such that for every G_1,G_2 in F, the intersection graph G_1∩G_2 contains a copy of K_t. Is it true that g_{K_t}(n)=2^{\binom{n}{2}-\binom{t}{2}} for all 4≤t≤n?
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, for every t≥4 and n≥t, is the 'trivial' family consisting of all graphs on [n] that contain a fixed copy of K_t always a largest possible K_t-intersecting family?
justification: The draft is clearly targeting Section 4’s Conjecture 4.1. Section 4 first defines H-intersecting families and the extremal function g_H(n), then states exactly the K_t specialization with the range 4≤t≤n and the formula g_{K_t}(n)=2^{\binom{n}{2}-\binom{t}{2}}. The nearby Proposition 4.2 and Conjecture 4.3 are not the same problem: they replace the condition 'G_1∩G_2 contains a copy of K_t' by the stronger/broader chromatic-number condition 'χ(G_1∩G_2)≥t'. The paragraph immediately after Conjecture 4.1 also provides important scope context by noting that Berger and Zhao proved the case t=4, leaving t≥5 open in the paper’s discussion.
